author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Environmental Protection Agency said Monday it is repealing rules that limit greenhouse-gas emissions from coal- and natural-gas-fired power plants, the Associated Press reported.

The agency also proposed a separate step that could prevent future administrations from regulating climate pollution from power plants. The repeal is expected to take effect after publication in the Federal Register, and environmental groups are preparing legal challenges.

The EPA said the rollback would save industry more than $300 billion in costs and give utilities more flexibility in deciding how to supply electricity. Environmental and public-health groups said removing the limits could increase pollution and harm communities.

The Associated Press reported that coal, gas and oil-fired power plants account for about one-quarter of the nation’s climate pollution. The EPA’s separate proposal is expected to be finalized next year if it survives the rulemaking process.

The announcements came as EPA and other U.S. energy officials hosted a G20 ministerial meeting in Houston. The changes represent a major shift in federal power-plant regulation and are likely to remain contested in court and in Congress.
dek: The agency says the rollback will cut industry costs, while environmental groups promise legal challenges and warn of broader pollution impacts.
headline: EPA moves to repeal power-plant climate rule, setting up court fights
